message.content:
**The United States Declaration of Independence** was adopted by the Continental Congress on **July 4, 1776**, but the formal signing ceremony took place on **August 2, 1776**.  
A total of **56 men** signed the document, representing the thirteen colonies. Below is the full list of signers, grouped by colony:

| Colony | Signers |
|--------|---------|
| **Delaware** | George Read, Caesar Rodney, George Calvert |
| **Pennsylvania** | John Morton, George Clymer, Benjamin Franklin, Robert Morris, George Taylor, James Smith |
| **New Jersey** | William Franklin, John Witherspoon, Francis Hopkinson, John Hart, Abraham Clark |
| **Georgia** | Button Gwinnett, Lyman Hall, George Walton |
| **Connecticut** | Roger Sherman, Samuel Huntington, William Williams, Oliver Wolcott |
| **Massachusetts** | John Hancock, Samuel Adams, Joseph Warren, John Adams, Paul Revere, John Hancock (again), John Hancock (again) – *[Note: John Hancock’s signature is famously large; he is listed once]* |
| **Maryland** | Charles Carroll of Carrollton, Samuel Chase, William Paca, Thomas Stone, Charles Carroll of Carrollton (again) – *[Note: Charles Carroll’s signature is the longest]* |
| **South Carolina** | Edward Rutledge, Thomas Heyward Jr., William Hooper, John Rutledge |
| **New Hampshire** | Josiah Bartlett, William Whipple, Matthew Thornton |
| **Virginia** | Benjamin Harrison, Thomas Jefferson, James Madison, Richard Henry Lee, Francis Lightfoot Lee, Carter Braxton |
| **New York** | Philip Livingston, Francis Lewis, Lewis Morris |
| **North Carolina** | William Hooper, Joseph Hewes, John Penn |
| **Rhode Island** | Stephen Hopkins, William Ellery, Roger Williams |

### Quick Facts

- **Total signers:** 56  
- **First signer (by order of appearance):** John Hancock (his large signature is a hallmark of the document).  
- **Longest signature:** Charles Carroll of Carrollton (the signature of the only Catholic signer).  
- **Most signatures by a single colony:** Pennsylvania (7 signers).  
- **Least signatures by a single colony:** Georgia (3 signers).  

These men were delegates to the Continental Congress and represented the collective resolve of the thirteen colonies to break away from British rule. Their signatures made the Declaration an official act of independence.
